- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update & Disclosure Letter

Before the issue-by-issue analysis, a framing point that colours the whole package.

**The "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing is not binding and should be rejected as framing.** The preamble asserts the terms were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "market standard," and are "not intended to be re-opened." Per our own playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3), none of that is substantive: a position is not agreed, pre-cleared or required just because the other side's document says so. I have no record of Amelia Frost authorising any of these fallbacks, and the "market standard 10–20% cap / 1% basket / 12–18 month" recitation is advocacy, not law. Treat the entire package as an opening seller draft, not a done deal.

Now the material departures.

---

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a *conditional* fallback usable **only** with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **none has been given.**

Do not be lulled because 4,800,000 happens to equal our fallback number. A matching number is not clearance (sec 6.3). **Push back to 25% / 6,000,000** unless and until Frost authorises the fallback in writing against this specific draft.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recover only the **excess** above the basket.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.

Three departures, all adverse: de minimis 5x too high, basket 5x too high, and a "deductible/excess-only" mechanic instead of our first-dollar (tipping-basket) recovery. **Push back on all three.**

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; and a sweeper that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all** Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a Frost-approved fallback only (**no approval given**). Fundamental/Title/Tax etc. must stay in **separate regimes**.

Two problems. First, **restore 24 months** — 18 is not cleared, and again a matching fallback number ≠ authority. Second, the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweeper is a **hidden general-regime override** that would drag Fundamental, Title and Tax into the short general clock. **Reject the sweeper**; insist the drafting ring-fences each regime.

## 4. Fundamental / Title regime — "administrative simplicity"
**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general.
**Playbook:** separate regime — **100% cap, minimum six years**, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

This is one of the most damaging asks in the package. Collapsing title/capacity into a 20% cap and 18-month clock would leave us under-protected on the very things (do we actually own the shares?) that should be fullest. **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to halve our title protection.

## 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance — Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** these apply to **all Claims of any nature.**
**Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable — and **no one may waive this.**

"All Claims of any nature" would sweep in fraud. **Insert the fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out** across every limitation, cap, basket, time bar, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. This is non-negotiable and non-waivable under our playbook.

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** general/deemed disclosure of the **entire data room** (DD-002 to DD-012) plus the Accounts, statutory registers and **publicly searchable records.**
**Playbook:** require **specific fair disclosure**; **reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.**

This is a direct hit on our playbook. A deemed "everything in the data room is disclosed" standard guts the warranties. **Reject** paras 1.1 and 1.2's deemed/general sweep; require that only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** (with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope) qualify. Note that para 1.4 (no admission of breach/liability/materiality) combined with blanket disclosure is doubly adverse.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge of, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.**
**Playbook:** **delete** blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

This is the "constructive/imputed knowledge" and "deemed discoverable" bar we must strike. It pairs with the deemed-disclosure clause above to double-count. **Delete** the blanket exclusion and the "discoverable" limb entirely. If any actual-knowledge qualifier survives, it must be tied to named individuals' actual knowledge and expressly **not** apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied **on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure para 2:** confirms **no final consent** and **no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at the letter date.

**Playbook:** require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is **insufficient** for a material customer.

Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — plainly material. The seller's own disclosure confirms the gap. **Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent **with satisfied conditions** a Completion condition, not a reasonable-endeavours/delivery formality.

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2 / 7
**Seller:** release to be provided **following Completion**.
**Disclosure para 3:** ~AUD 3,200,000 still outstanding, **no discharge** of security included.

**Playbook:** require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (no approval given).

A bare "release following Completion" leaves us owning a company whose bank security may still be live. **Push back:** direct payout from completion funds and security releases effective at Completion. If seller insists on post-completion mechanics, we need an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Frost sign-off — neither exists. Also tie this to the debt-free/cash-free premise: the AUD 3.2m must be cleared, not left to us.

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow / Disclosure para 5
**Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," **not itemised** in the funds flow. On-costs unaddressed.
**Playbook:** the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a **specific line item or seller-funded**; the funds flow must **not silently exclude** them.

The risk is that "not itemised / a matter for the Seller" quietly leaves the economic burden — or the on-costs (payroll tax, super) — with the company (and so us) post-Completion. **Push back:** make it an explicit line item or an express seller-funded/indemnified obligation **inclusive of on-costs**, and confirm the funds flow reconciles.

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 / Disclosure para 4
**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate."
**Playbook:** **broaden** the narrow indemnity while **preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is **not independently verified either way**.

Disclosure para 4 confirms DD-004 cl 7.3 withholds transfer of **SOW3 Project Materials** until **every SOW3 fee** is cleared, and there's **no receipt/confirmatory assignment** in the data room — so the IP in those deliverables may not have validly transferred. A pure-dollar indemnity capped at the fee doesn't cover that IP-title risk. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to the IP/assignment consequences (not just the AUD 180k payment), while preserving the cure of paying the SOW3 fees. Don't accept the AUD 180,000 as established — it's unverified.

## 12. Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure para 6 (DD-006)
**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
**Disclosure para 6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); **cannot yet establish** access, scope, or notification duty.

**Playbook:** **preserve logs, investigate, require updates**; assume **NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand** in either direction.

I agree there's no confirmed breach — so **don't overclaim** a breach or a loss figure. But equally **don't accept the seller's "not material" characterisation** as a conclusion. **Push back:** specific interim covenants requiring log preservation, continued investigation, and prompt updates to the Buyer, plus a targeted indemnity for liabilities arising from the incident. Treat as open, not closed, in both directions.

## 13. Sandbar renewals — Disclosure para 8
**Seller:** three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
**Playbook:** **assess**; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally no automatic acceptance.

Disclosure para 8 concedes it's **not stated** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. So the seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported. **Push back:** request the renewal terms (term, termination rights, accrual) to assess. We do **not** reflexively treat them as Debt/price reduction, but we don't accept the ordinary-course characterisation on assertion either.

## 14. Title evidence — Clause / Disclosure para 10 (DD-012)
**Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
**Playbook:** require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.**

The seller's own para 10 admits DD-012 "identifies the source relied on" and that the Buyer hasn't done its own verification. **Push back:** require independent verification — ASIC/register searches obtained by us, the share certificate(s), evidence of no encumbrances over the shares, and corporate authority for the sale. An internal register the seller controls is not sufficient title proof. This ties back to Issue 4 — title warranties must sit in the 100%/six-year regime.

## 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume **no unlimited liability and no resolution**. Keep Tax/IP categories **separate**; no hidden general-regime override.

This is another attempt to fold separate categories (and their longer tax clocks) into the 18-month / 20% general cage. **Reject:** Tax and IP are unresolved and must be negotiated as separate regimes, not deemed "settled" by cross-reference.

## Minor / watch items
- **Office lease (para 7):** notification obligation, not consent — seller's reading looks right, but confirm the notification is actually given.
- **Mossvale (para 9):** assignment restriction; seller says share sale doesn't trigger consent — plausible, but verify the clause wording ourselves rather than accept the characterisation.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

**Hold the line / revert to playbook baseline:**
1. Cap: restore **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (20% is not authorised; matching number ≠ clearance).
2. Thresholds: **AUD 5,000** de minimis, **AUD 50,000** basket, **first-dollar** recovery (not excess-only).
3. Time: restore **24 months** general (18 not authorised); **delete** the "applies to all Claims" sweeper.

**Reject outright:**
4. Collapsing **Title/Capacity** into general cap/time — keep **100% cap / six years / outside basket & knowledge bar**.
5. Blanket + "discoverable" **buyer-knowledge** exclusion (Cl 8.3).
6. **Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure** (para 1.1–1.2) — require specific fair disclosure.
7. Tax/IP "settled under general regime" — keep **separate and open**.

**Insert / insist:**
8. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** across all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance — non-waivable.
9. **Bluefen**: effective consent **with satisfied 11.3 conditions** as a Completion condition (not reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery).
10. **Riverlark**: current payout, direct repayment from completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking **+ Frost approval**.
11. **Bonuses**: AUD 420,000 **plus on-costs** as explicit line item or seller-funded; funds flow must reconcile.
12. **Ironquay**: broaden indemnity to IP/assignment risk, preserve SOW3 cure; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
13. **DD-006 incident**: log preservation, investigation and update covenants + targeted indemnity; resist "not material" conclusion without conceding a breach.
14. **Title**: independent verification (register searches, certificates, no-encumbrance and authority evidence); DD-012 is not sufficient.

**Assess, don't concede:**
15. **Sandbar** AUD 330,000: obtain terms; no automatic Debt/price deduction, but no automatic "ordinary course" acceptance either.
16. Verify **lease notification** and **Mossvale** wording ourselves.

**Escalation flags for the deal team:** The 20% cap and 18-month period both require **Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft** before we could even offer them as fallbacks — I have no record either has been given. Do not let the "FINAL / agreed / pre-cleared" framing substitute for our own authority process.

One caveat on my own analysis: my comments rest on the seller's summaries and the disclosure letter as drafted; please have the deal team confirm the underlying DD-002–DD-012 documents and the actual SPA clause wording, since the seller's characterisations (e.g. "ordinary course," "not material," "adequate") are advocacy, not verified fact.
